title: Trend of Youths Radicalising via Gaming, Chat and Social Media Platforms
what_it_is: Trend of Youths Radicalising via Gaming, Chat and Social Media Platforms

sections.label: Self-radicalised youth ISA detentions
sections.summary: From 2007 to 2014, one self-radicalised youth aged 20 was detained under the ISA; since 2015, 11 aged 15 to 20 were detained or given Restriction Orders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: From 2007 to 2014, only one self-radicalised youth, aged 20, was detained under the Internal Security Act (ISA).

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Since 2015, there have been 11 self-radicalised youths aged between 15 and 20 who were detained or issued with Restriction Orders under the ISA.

sections.label: Broadcasting Act and online harms
sections.summary: Under the amended Broadcasting Act effective 1 February 2023, IMDA can direct social media services to disable access to content instructing or advocating terrorism or violence, and MHA will introduce legislation on online criminal harms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Separately, under the amended Broadcasting Act which took effect on 1 February 2023, the Info-communications Media Development Authority can direct social media services to disable access to content instructing or advocating terrorism or violence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) will also be introducing later this year, legislation to combat online criminal harms, which will cover content that incites terror-related activities.

sections.label: Community partners youth outreach
sections.summary: They work with community partners such as RRG and ACG, which reach out to youths and families for sessions and forums.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Like what I shared earlier, we work with community partners, such as RRG and ACG, where they reach out to youths and families to have sessions and forums.

sections.label: Media and MOE outreach efforts
sections.summary: They invite media for coverage, work with MOE schools and IHLs, and in 2022 ISD organised at least 69 outreach events for over 2,300 participants, engaging principals, educators, student leaders, and over 350 school counsellors and student welfare officers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: When doing these, we also asked the media, we invited the media and we usually have good media coverage to share the messages.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: That is one and we also work with our Government agencies such as the Ministry of Education (MOE) – a key partner of our counterterrorism and counter-radicalisation efforts, where we look at how we collaborate with MOE schools and Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) on such efforts.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: For example, in 2022, ISD organised at least 69 counterterrorism and counter-radicalisation outreach events, both online and in-person for more than 2,300 participants, including student leaders, educators and other school staff.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We also engage the principals, educators and student leaders and we also work with school counsellors and student welfare officers – as of 2022, over 350 school counsellors and school student welfare officers.
